clue.text: Small sailor pursuing large hunk

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the sailor follows the large

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A little seaman trails after a big, handsome man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' puts AB after L, so the order is S, L, AB.
explanation.definitionFit: A slab is a thick, solid chunk of something, just as a hunk is.

clue.text: Perhaps doctor's responsibility is to examine piles?

parts.note: to case a place is to examine it closely, as a burglar does
a load, as in loads of money, means piles or lots

explanation.surface: A doctor wondering whether checking haemorrhoids counts as part of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piles' looks medical in a clue about a doctor, but it just means a great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's caseload is the set of patients they are responsible for; 'Perhaps' marks the doctor as one example of such a professional.

clue.text: Mediocre housing officers finally get engaged

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the mediocre word contains the letter

parts.note: meh is an informal word for mediocre or unremarkable

indicators.note: finally means taking the last letter of officers

explanation.surface: Officers from an unremarkable housing estate finally decide to get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' reads as homes for officers but signals containment: S goes inside MEH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh when their teeth interlock, which is to engage with each other.

clue.text: Shy guards gather briefly, having a row

indicators.note: guards means the throwing word surrounds the shortened gathering word

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to sling

indicators.note: briefly means the word for gather is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to cull is to gather or pick, as in culling facts

explanation.surface: A timid person shields a quick get-together while in the middle of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter; 'guards' puts the result inside the word for shy. 'row' is the boating word, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculling is propelling a boat with oars, which is rowing.

clue.text: Time to leave African capital, working in harmony

indicators.note: to leave means the time letter is dropped from the capital

parts.note: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Time to depart an African capital, everyone cooperating nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to leave' sounds like a departure but means drop T from TUNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in unison is to act together in agreement, as voices singing the same note.

clue.text: Cook modest Arab dishes

indicators.note: cook in the sense of cooking the books, falsifying, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to prepare some simple Middle Eastern food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishes' looks like food in a cooking clue, but here means attractive people.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes is slang for good-looking people, and dreamboats are very attractive people.

clue.text: Some jovial intellectuals beam

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few cheerful academics are smiling broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' looks like a smile but is the structural timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A lintel is the horizontal beam spanning the top of a door or window.

clue.text: Philosopher regularly ignoring Mary Beard

indicators.note: regularly ignoring means every other letter of Mary Beard is skipped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A thinker repeatedly overlooks the classicist Mary Beard.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Beard is a well-known British classicist and broadcaster. A. J. Ayer was a British logical positivist philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: A. J. Ayer was a twentieth-century British philosopher, author of Language, Truth and Logic.

clue.text: Let learner driver move gradually

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate in Britain
to ease something is to move it slowly and carefully

explanation.surface: Allow a novice motorist to edge forward slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease a property is to rent it out, which is to let it.

clue.text: Engineer crying out for agreement

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer shouting out to get a deal agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Congruity is the quality of being consistent or in accord, a kind of agreement.

clue.text: Boozers pick up rubbish, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds are exchanged

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it
balls is slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Drinkers collecting litter, in Spooner's muddled words.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds gives BEAR HALLS, which is said like BEER HALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozers is British slang for pubs, and beer halls are large drinking places.

clue.text: Looking for more nuts, first off

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: dafter means sillier, more nuts

explanation.surface: A squirrel searching for extra nuts, first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' sounds like 'to begin with' but means drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be after something is to be seeking or looking for it.

clue.text: Italian food, craft gin and endless chocs

indicators.note: to craft is to make or shape, so the letters are fashioned into a new order
endless means the last letter of chocs is removed

explanation.surface: A shopping list of artisanal gin and chocolates without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims chocs to CHOC, and 'craft' rearranges GIN plus CHOC. 'craft gin' looks like a trendy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings, usually made from potato.

clue.text: Clumsy wit upset discontented killjoy

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for wit is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit

indicators.note: discontented means the contents are removed, leaving only the outer letters of killjoy

explanation.surface: An awkward joker overturns an unhappy spoilsport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns WAG into GAW; 'discontented' empties killjoy to KY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawky describes someone awkward and ungainly in movement, that is, clumsy.

clue.text: Fellow convent dweller is involved in tattoos and riddles

parts.note: co- as a prefix means fellow, as in co-worker
a nun lives in a convent
a tattoo is a drumbeat, so one who drums is involved in tattoos

explanation.surface: A fellow nun is mixed up in body art and puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoos' suggests body ink but means drum signals, as in a military tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling question or riddle.

clue.text: Clouds of particles and gas obscure bus lane

indicators.note: to obscure is to muddle or confuse, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Exhaust fumes hiding a lane reserved for buses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulae are interstellar clouds of dust and gas; this is the anglicised plural.

clue.text: Tail of famous clownfish

indicators.note: tail of means taking the last letter of famous

parts.note: a prat is a fool or clown

explanation.surface: The tail fin of a well-known clownfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clownfish' looks like one word but splits into clown and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Make broader jam-makers retreat

parts.note: the WI, Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation famous for making jam
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Jam-producers withdraw in order to expand.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation known for jam-making.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen something is to make it wider, broadening it.

clue.text: For instance, millions in profits for energy suppliers

indicators.note: in means the example word and the million go inside the profits

parts.note: gains are profits
as means for instance, as in 'a fruit such as'
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Energy companies making millions in profits, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted letters go in just after the first letter of the profits word; the answer is two words, 3 and 5.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas mains are the pipes that carry gas, a source of energy, to buildings.

clue.text: Most Greek wine is revolting and evil

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the letters are read backwards
most means all but the last letter of the wine is kept

parts.note: retsina is a resinated Greek wine

explanation.surface: Most Greek wine is disgusting and wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' trims RETSINA to RETSIN; RETSIN plus IS read backwards. 'revolting' looks like disgust but means turning back.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means wicked or threatening harm, that is, evil.

clue.text: Hate a Danish physicist after change of heart

indicators.note: after a change of heart, the physicist's central letters are switched round, rearranging the name

parts.note: Niels Bohr was a Danish physicist

explanation.surface: Someone comes to dislike a Danish scientist after changing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the middle O and H of BOHR, giving BHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to detest it, to hate it.

clue.text: Priestly dictator's loftier loft

indicators.note: dictator's suggests something dictated, spoken out for another to write

parts.note: loftier is higher, and a loft is an attic

explanation.surface: A tyrant's taller roof space.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGHER ATTIC, spoken, is said like HIERATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieratic means relating to priests, especially the priestly script of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Tackle coverage of unknown weather features

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic unknowns
fronts are boundaries between air masses on weather maps

explanation.surface: Reporting on the unseen features of tomorrow's weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' is slang for male genitals, not fishing or football gear. Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are men's underpants, which cover a man's private parts, jokingly called his tackle.

clue.text: Small and extremely radioactive speck of dust

indicators.note: extremely means the outer letters of radioactive are taken

parts.note: a mote is a tiny particle of dust

explanation.surface: A tiny, very radioactive particle of dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote chance is a slight or small one.

clue.text: Local tinned potatoes in Delhi?

indicators.note: in Delhi tells you the potatoes are named in Hindi and placed in the tin letters, as tinned food sits in its can

parts.note: tinned suggests tin, whose chemical symbol is Sn
aloo is the Hindi word for potatoes, familiar from Indian menus

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood shop sells canned potatoes in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delhi?' tells you to use the Hindi word, ALOO; 'tinned' supplies Sn, the chemical symbol for tin. A saloon was the smarter bar of a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Local is British slang for a nearby pub, and the saloon is a bar in a pub.

clue.text: Beginning new push to the summit

parts.note: an ascent is a climb to the top

explanation.surface: Starting a fresh attempt to reach the mountaintop.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, beginning to develop.

clue.text: Wayward emu regularly hiding object

indicators.note: hiding means the answer is concealed within the preceding words, running across them

explanation.surface: An errant emu often hides some item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal but is just fodder; 'object' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance.

clue.text: Five ducks plunged into water and perished

indicators.note: ducks means the five letter ducks out, dodging away from the word

parts.note: to dive is to plunge into water
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A handful of ducks dived into a pond and died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like birds but is a verb: V ducks out of DIVED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean having come to the end of life.

clue.text: Jockey let a horse give up

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre or shuffle for position, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A rider allows a horse to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is to become discouraged and stop trying, to give up.

clue.text: Cannabis and ecstasy in prison

indicators.note: in means the drug letter is put inside the prison letters

parts.note: HMP, Her Majesty's Prison, prefixes British prison names
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs being smuggled into a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: HMP (Her Majesty's Prison) is the British prefix for jails, as in HMP Wandsworth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is the cannabis plant.

clue.text: Donald, president of America, wearing turtleneck inside out

indicators.note: wearing means the American letters are inside the garment letters
inside out means the inside is removed, keeping the outer letters of turtleneck

parts.note: US is America

explanation.surface: A US president, Donald, in a turtleneck worn inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donald, president of America' looks like Trump; 'of America' is wordplay. Donald Tusk was President of the European Council.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Tusk, former Polish prime minister, served as President of the European Council.

clue.text: Unguardedly messages one back, opening spontaneously

indicators.note: unguardedly means the guards at each end are removed

parts.note: texts are messages sent by phone

indicators.note: back means the word for one is read in reverse

parts.note: one, as a speaker's way of referring to oneself, means me
a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: Carelessly sending texts back to someone, speaking off the cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unguardedly' strips TEXTS to EXT; 'back' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means without preparation, off the cuff, which is spontaneously.

clue.text: See 18
